{{MEinfobox|name=Protection|cg=Protection.png}}'''Protection''' and its variants are positive status effects which reduce the damage dealt to the target.

{{StatusEffect|Protection|b}} causes Skill damage to be decreased by 10% per Count (to a maximum of 100% or taking no Skill damage), and expires at the end of the turn.
There are three types of Protection for a total of eleven effects: 
* The standard {{StatusEffect|Protection|b}}, which decreases all damage taken.
* Three {{StatusEffect|Slash Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Pierce Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Blunt Protection|x}} Damage Type Protection that decrease [[Slash]], [[Pierce]] and [[Blunt]] damage respectively.
* Seven {{StatusEffect|Wrath Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Lust Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Sloth Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Gluttony Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Gloom Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Pride Protection|x}}{{StatusEffect|Envy Protection|x}} Sin Affinity Fragilities that decrease damage from each [[Sin]] Affinity.

Some status effects (e.g. {{StatusEffect|Blessing (E.G.O Gift)|b}} or {{StatusEffect|Ridiculous Grit (Outis)|b}}) decrease resistances (causing units to take less damage) and function similarly to Protection, but apply to a different part of the [[Damage Formula|damage calculation formula]]. 

==Strengths & Weaknesses==
{{StatusEffect|Protection|b}} is a powerful status effect that can significantly decrease damage taken. Its main limitation is that it expires at Turn End, and that Protection does not prevent fixed damage, meaning status effects like {{StatusEffect|Bleed|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Burn|d}} will still deal damage. This means enemies that employ many protective buffs can still be dealt significant damage through status effects. 

Different types of Protection can be stacked for additive bonuses. For example, an enemy with 3 {{StatusEffect|Protection|b}} and 3 {{StatusEffect|Slash Protection|b}} would take -60% damage from Slash Skills that turn. 

It is worth noting that different types of Protection (and all other damage modifiers, such as {{StatusEffect|Damage Up|b}} and Skill conditionals) can stack and counteract each other, and will continue to change the damage modifier. For example, units with many offensive buffs may be able to override protective buffs on their targets, as the values are added together.
